cohort: 150 neonates born at the second stage of delivery in an obstetric theatre via instrumental delivery (forceps or vacuum) or emergency caesarian section.
finding: Shoulder dystocia and neonatal injury were statistically significantly less in neonates born via forceps delivery compared to vacuum or emergency caesarian section for second-stage delivery.
mod_finding: Forceps delivery emerged as a relatively safer method, being associated with statistically significantly less shoulder dystocia and neonatal injury compared to vacuum or emergency caesarian section.
